🤖 Teaching reasoning LLMs to control real-world robots using purely reinforcement learning in simulation just got a massive upgrade! 

MIT Han Lab’s PEAR is a brand-new post-training engine built to conquer the notorious simulation-to-real bottleneck in physical AI. It lets you train large reasoning models natively on robotic hardware with zero human demonstrations required. 

Here is how PEAR makes it happen:

⚡ Fully Asynchronous RL Scaling: Powered by verl with GRPO, dynamic sampling, and score centering.
🚀 High-Throughput Infrastructure: Maximizes memory efficiency using MTP speculative decoding, LMCache CPU-offloaded KV cache, FSDP, and sequence parallelism.
🔄 Heterogeneous Simulation: Seamlessly runs MuJoCo on CPUs and Isaac Sim on GPUs on the same Ray cluster.
🛠️ Optimized Deployment: Supports vLLM server deployment on modern NVIDIA hardware like the RTX 5090 and GB300 for real-world robot agent loops.

Whether you are training open 27B reasoning models for complex manipulation tasks in simulation or deploying optimized agents to edge-adjacent hardware, PEAR bridges the gap between simulated reasoning and physical execution. 

Check out the repository and start building today:
https://github.com/mit-han-lab/pear

Tired of paying for expensive cloud-based SaaS wrappers just to chop your long-form videos into TikToks and Reels? 

Meet NeonClipping: an open-source, local video clipping engine that converts long YouTube streams, Twitch VODs, and local MP4 files into viral 9:16 vertical clips entirely on your own hardware. 

No cloud uploads. No subscription fees. 100% privacy.

Powered by FastAPI, OpenAI Whisper for speech recognition, and Ollama for local LLM scoring, NeonClipping automates your entire short-form content pipeline locally.

🔥 Key Features:
- Dual highlight discovery modes combining audio-jump signals, 2-4 kHz raised-voice detection, OpenCV optical flow motion analysis, and local LLM scoring.
- 11 native layout engines with facecam presets, custom bounding boxes, blurred fills, and multi-platform safe zones.
- Adaptive local feedback learning loop using ridge regression to tune signal weights based on your star ratings.
- Support for Hinglish transliteration, word-timed subtitles (GTA Neon and Hormozi styles), and blazing-fast NVENC hardware acceleration.

Whether you are a developer looking for an architectural blueprint to integrate local ML models with FFmpeg, or a creator wanting to automate your video repurposing pipeline for free, this stack delivers.

👉 Check out the repository and start clipping locally:
https://github.com/iamajmeena/neonclipping

Stuck choosing between cutting-edge 3D Gaussian splatting and nostalgic pixel-art aesthetics? You no longer have to choose. 🎨✨

Ink Studio bridges the gap by delivering a complete JavaScript toolkit for procedural sculpting, simulation, and low-fi 3D baking.

Traditional 3D pipelines are heavy, manual, and completely miss the mark when you want stylized, retro, or low-fi computer vision assets. Ink Studio solves this scarcity head-on. It allows you to programmatically sculpt signed-distance solids in JavaScript, bake them straight into pixel-art Gaussian splats, animate puppets, run physics simulations, and render the output without bloated software overhead.

Here is what makes it a game-changer for your stack:
• SDF Sculpting & Adaptive Sampling: Intelligently concentrates splats on bevels and silhouettes while thinning flat areas.
• Native Volumetric Baking: Turns solids into 16-float-per-splat Gaussian data arrays carrying covariance matrices, colors, and simulation metadata.
• Comprehensive Simulation Engine: Handles particle systems, cloth, hair, physics, live sun relighting, and art-directed shadow ramps.
• Zero Runtime Dependency Design: Features dual-mode execution supporting headless Node.js CLI rendering and browser-based WebGL 2 embedding.

Whether you are building headless procedural world generators in Node or generating retro-styled 3D assets and animated sprite atlases for web-based games, this is your code-first alternative to manual 3D modeling. 🚀

Check out the repository and start building:
https://github.com/siliconjungle/shapeshift-labs-ink-studio

Tired of flying blind when inspecting what Android apps are doing in the background? 🕵️‍♂️📱

Meet Jiumi—an open-source Android activity and privacy monitoring tool that tracks background behaviors, permission accesses, and network traffic locally without ever requiring root access. By leveraging shell-level debugging APIs, wireless debugging, and Shizuku, Jiumi gives you deep visibility into device telemetry without the headache of custom ROM flashing.

Here is what makes it a must-have in your toolkit:

⚡ Root-less Shell Probing: Gather system telemetry including AppOps permission histories, connection tables, Perfetto system traces, and event logs using wireless debugging or Shizuku.
🛡️ Comprehensive Action Management: Control app permissions, toggle built-in firewall-based network access without VPN overhead, disable or enable packages, and safely manage preloaded system apps.
📊 Local Telemetry & Audit Exports: Track 12 categories and 56 types of app behaviors entirely on-device, with options to export logs into ZIP bundles containing CSV files for deep analysis.
🌐 Optional DNS Logging: Capture and forward DNS queries using a local VPN loopback to map out domain-level network activities for specific applications.

Whether you are a developer auditing your own app's interactions with the Android OS, a mobile QA engineer verifying permission constraints, or a security researcher analyzing telemetry calls, Jiumi streamlines the entire audit workflow. Plus, the codebase serves as a clean architectural reference for building advanced non-root system monitoring tools.

Check out the repository and start inspecting your app telemetry today:
https://github.com/ybblab/Jiumi
